headline: Gulshan home of former President Sahabuddin being prepared for his return
summary: Cleaning and painting work is underway at the private residence of the recently resigned President, who is expected to return home soon.
details: Following the resignation of President Md. Sahabuddin, cleaning and renovation work has begun at his private residence on Road 123 in Gulshan, Dhaka.
The ground floor sitting area is being repainted, and furniture is being cleaned to prepare for his arrival.
The building manager, Kabir Hossain, stated that while the exact date of return is unknown, they have been instructed to ensure everything is clean and ready.
President Sahabuddin resigned on Friday, citing illness as the reason for leaving the office nearly 21 months before his term was set to end in April 2028.
He had taken office as the 22nd President of Bangladesh on April 24, 2023, after being elected unopposed on an Awami League nomination.
His resignation letter was submitted to the Speaker of the National Parliament, Hafiz Uddin Ahmed, who then announced the transition of presidential duties according to the constitution.
Family belongings have already been moved to the Gulshan residence, and the house is being made habitable for his return from Bangabhaban.
caption:
Cleaning and painting are underway at the Gulshan home of former President Md. Sahabuddin as he prepares to return.

Following the resignation of President Md. Sahabuddin, cleaning and renovation work has begun at his private residence on Road 123 in Gulshan, Dhaka.

The ground floor sitting area is being repainted, and furniture is being cleaned to prepare for his arrival.

The building manager, Kabir Hossain, stated that while the exact date of return is unknown, they have been instructed to ensure everything is clean and ready.

President Sahabuddin resigned on Friday, citing illness as the reason for leaving the office nearly 21 months before his term was set to end in April 2028.

He had taken office as the 22nd President of Bangladesh on April 24, 2023, after being elected unopposed on an Awami League nomination.

His resignation letter was submitted to the Speaker of the National Parliament, Hafiz Uddin Ahmed, who then announced the transition of presidential duties according to the constitution.

Family belongings have already been moved to the Gulshan residence, and the house is being made habitable for his return from Bangabhaban.

headline_marked: BGB [[foils BSF bid to push 6 people]] into Bangladesh
headline: BGB foils BSF bid to push 6 people into Bangladesh
summary: Border Guard Bangladesh prevented the entry of four men and two women at the Maheshpur border in Jhenaidah early today.
details: Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) has claimed that India's Border Security Force (BSF) attempted to push six individuals—four men and two women—into Bangladesh early today.
The incident occurred around 5:10 am in the Samanta Border Outpost (BOP) area of Maheshpur upazila in Jhenaidah.
According to a BGB press release, members of the BSF Battalion-59 from Singamora Camp tried to push the individuals through a gate adjacent to border pillar 55/MP.
A BGB patrol detected the attempt before the individuals could enter Bangladesh and successfully prevented their entry.
The six individuals are currently staying about 30 yards inside Indian territory from the zero line, and the BGB has communicated the matter to the BSF.
Lt Col Md Rafiqul Alam, Commanding Officer of BGB Maheshpur Battalion-58, stated that the force remains on maximum alert to prevent illegal infiltration and maintain peace in border areas.
caption:
BGB stopped 6 people from being pushed into Bangladesh by India's BSF early this morning.

Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) has claimed that India's Border Security Force (BSF) attempted to push six individuals—four men and two women—into Bangladesh early today.

The incident occurred around 5:10 am in the Samanta Border Outpost (BOP) area of Maheshpur upazila in Jhenaidah.

According to a BGB press release, members of the BSF Battalion-59 from Singamora Camp tried to push the individuals through a gate adjacent to border pillar 55/MP.

A BGB patrol detected the attempt before the individuals could enter Bangladesh and successfully prevented their entry.

The six individuals are currently staying about 30 yards inside Indian territory from the zero line, and the BGB has communicated the matter to the BSF.

Lt Col Md Rafiqul Alam, Commanding Officer of BGB Maheshpur Battalion-58, stated that the force remains on maximum alert to prevent illegal infiltration and maintain peace in border areas.
